subject: On‑prem VPC fabric: orchestration, control/data ownership, and pilot runbook

Subject: On‑prem VPC fabric kickoff and initial questions

Markus,

Thanks for making time. NexaLabs is standing up a small pilot to host Redwood Private behind our colo VPC. We want to validate the control/data separation patterns you use (control plane in customer VPC to the extent possible, data plane colocated on our rack fabric), and confirm the production cutover checklist for tenant isolation and egress proofing.

Two quick asks before the architecture review meeting:
- Can you confirm whether the control plane components require outbound internet egress, or if they can be fully routed through our transit VPC?
- Are there specific KV cache or KV-proxy placement constraints we should be aware of for latency-sensitive workloads?

We also need a short list of required evidence (certs, audit logs, network tagging) we should prepare in advance of the pilot.

Thanks,
Alex Chang
Infrastructure Lead 
NexaLabs

Subject: Re: On‑prem VPC fabric kickoff and initial questions

Alex — thanks, and great questions. I attached a short reference pack (PDF) and an initial pilot runbook (MD) that outline our recommended topology and the handoff points. High level answers:

1) Control plane egress: control-plane components (agent registration, metrics push, and artifact fetch) can be configured to use your transit VPC — we do not require direct public internet egress for the control plane. We also support an outbound proxy configuration for artifact retrieval if you need to route through a corporate gateway.

2) KV cache / proxy placement: for low-latency inference, place the KV-proxy in the same rack pod as the runtime nodes. The reference diagrams show an optional sidecar vs dedicated proxy pool; for pilot scale I recommend a small dedicated proxy pool per tenant-pod to simplify failover testing.

Evidence checklist (short):
- TLS certs for inter-cluster control channels (mutual TLS)
- Inventory of public/private IPs and routing table snapshots
- Proof of KMS integration for customer-managed keys (if requested)
- Sample flow logs (VPC flow + application-level) for at least one day of simulated load

Action items for the sync on Friday:
- Walk reference diagrams (I will present)
- Agree on runbook cutover steps and rollback gates
- Decide on KV-proxy sizing for pilot workload (latency SLA target: 50ms p95 per inference call)

I attached: 1) 20260707_markus_vpc_reference_diagrams.pdf 2) pilot_runbook_v0.3.md

—Markus Klein
Head of Deployments (Redwood Inference)

Alex / Markus — quick clarifications from a compliance and customer-safety perspective before Friday's walkthrough:

- SLA & data residency: confirm whether the pilot's logs/artifacts remain within NexaLabs' VPC by default (we need an explicit statement for sales procurement). If KMS is customer-managed, note the rotation cadence and access control model in the runbook.
- Audit evidence: please provide the schema/fields for the sample flow logs we asked for. We will need timestamps, source/dest CIDR labels, and an annotation for any NAT translation.
- Egress gating: for the agent bootstrap path, include a control-plane fallback policy in the runbook that pins to a regional relay if the primary transit is not available. That reduces blast radius during network flaps.

I also propose adding an extra rollback gate: after routing cutover but before tenant traffic ramp, run an I/O validation (KV read/write at 99pct success for 5 min) — add this as step 6 in the runbook.

Thanks — see you on Friday.

Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance (Redwood Inference)
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
